claims.explanation: WZ-4002 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling. Sensitive lines include those with EGFR mutations (HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270) and ERBB2/ERBB3 alterations (SNUC5), while resistant lines often have mutations in downstream effectors (KRAS, BRAF, NRAS, NF1, PTEN) that bypass receptor inhibition. Thus, activating mutations in EGFR/ERBB2 or high expression of these receptors predict sensitivity, whereas mutations that activate MAPK/PI3K pathways downstream confer resistance.

features.basis: Activating EGFR mutations sensitize to EGFR inhibitors; observed in sensitive lines HCC4006, NCIH1650, KYSE270.
ERBB2 kinase domain mutations can be sensitive to ERBB2 inhibitors; SNUC5 has ERBB3 mutation but ERBB2 pathway activation may sensitize.
High EGFR expression increases dependence on EGFR signaling; sensitive lines include lung and esophageal squamous lines.
ERBB2 overexpression predicts response to ERBB2-targeted inhibitors.
KRAS mutations activate downstream MAPK signaling, bypassing EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition; observed in resistant lines GSU_STOMACH, SNU410_PANCREAS, OV7_OVARY.
BRAF mutations activate MAPK pathway downstream of EGFR; observed in resistant lines LOXIMVI, K029AX, IGR37.
NRAS mutations activate downstream signaling; observed in resistant lines IPC298, KU1919.
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK pathway; observed in resistant lines KALS1, FTC133, S117, BICR6.
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT pathway; observed in resistant lines KALS1, FTC133, 786O, ZR751.
PIK3CA mutations activate PI3K pathway; observed in resistant lines HGC27, KYSE510, and some sensitive lines, but overall may reduce dependence on EGFR.
MAP2K1 mutation activates MEK/ERK downstream of EGFR; observed in resistant line NCIH1437.
MET mutation may provide alternative RTK signaling; observed in resistant line HGC27.
